title: Purple Cow
author: Seth Godin
blurb: Seth Godin opens with a simple picture. Driving through the countryside, you are charmed by cows at first. Soon they all look the same, and you stop seeing them. A purple cow, though, would stop you in your tracks. Godin argues that most products today are brown cows. The old formula of making something decent and buying lots of advertising no longer works, because people are flooded with choices and tune ads out. The answer is to build something remarkable, meaning worth making a remark about, right into the product itself. He explains why playing it safe is now the riskiest move, why very good is not good enough, and why you should design for the small group of eager early adopters who spread ideas to everyone else. Marketing, in his view, starts with the product, not after it.
